subtopic: TVM: real measurement vs analytical cost model
learningObjective: Explain why TVM (and its Ansor/AutoTVM descendants) rely on real hardware measurement rather than a pure analytical cost model to select schedules.
stem: TVM's schedule search relies on on-device measurement (feeding a learned cost model) rather than a pure analytical performance model. Which statement best captures the design rationale argued in the TVM paper?

options.text: Analytical models cannot express any form of loop tiling, so measurement is the only way to compare tiled schedules; without measurement TVM would be forced to emit only untiled code.

On modern accelerators, effective performance depends on hard-to-model factors (cache/coalescing, register pressure, instruction mix, compiler back-end choices) that closed-form models fail to rank reliably at fine granularity, so a measurement-driven (and learned) cost model is used to guide the search.
Measurement is used purely for reproducibility: since analytical models depend on constants that vary by driver version, TVM re-measures every kernel on every deployment to remove that dependency.
The paper argues that a sufficiently detailed analytical model is always superior; measurement is included only as a compatibility path for hardware without a published architecture manual.

explanation: TVM (and Ansor) argue that closed-form analytical models miss important microarchitectural effects. A learned cost model trained on measurements ranks candidates cheaply; a subset is then measured on-device to refine the model. The design accepts autotuning wall-clock time as a trade-off for high-quality schedules across many targets.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: analytical models can express tiling; the objection is about ranking accuracy, not expressibility.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: matches the paper's stated argument for measurement-based (learned) cost.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: reproducibility is not the stated motivation.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: the paper does not claim analytical models are always superior.

assumptions: Familiarity with the TVM paper's autotuning pipeline.
nonImplications: Does not imply autotuning is free; TVM explicitly accepts autotuning time as a trade-off.
Does not imply analytical models are removed; a learned cost model on top of measurements is analytical in a broad sense.
